findings.message: All four committed R entrypoints call setwd() without a directory argument and therefore are not directly runnable as committed.
The R scripts reference Master File of Data extraction_new.xlsx while the pinned repository stores Master File of Data extraction_New.xlsx; this fails on case-sensitive filesystems.
The reproducibility repository does not pin the R interpreter version needed to recreate the historical analysis environment.
The analysis depends on readxl, meta, dmetar and dplyr, but exact historical package versions are not fully pinned.

The scripts use meta::metaprop arguments such as comb.fixed, comb.random and byvar; exact package identity must be fixed before interpreting a successful rerun as historical computational reproduction.

proposedRepairs.description: Execute each script with the captured repository root as the working directory and neutralize the argument-less setwd() call in the reproduction harness.
proposedRepairs.rationale: The shim changes file-location setup only and does not alter data, model settings, estimands or statistical calculations.

proposedRepairs.description: Map the script-requested workbook basename to the exact captured workbook path with repository capitalization.
proposedRepairs.rationale: The repair resolves a case-sensitive path spelling difference while preserving the exact captured workbook bytes.
